candidates.source_excerpt: When multiple lanes in one direction are closed, a capacity analysis should be made to determine the number of lanes needed to accommodate motor vehicle traffic needs. Vehicular traffic should be moved over one lane at a time. As shown in Figure 6P-37, the tapers should be separated by a distance of 2L, with L being determined by the formulas in Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4.

candidates.source_excerpt: When a lane is closed on a multi-lane road for other than a mobile operation, a transition area containing a merging taper shall be used.

candidates.source_excerpt: A merging taper should be long enough to enable merging drivers to have adequate advance warning and sufficient length to adjust their speeds and merge into an adjacent lane before the downstream end of the transition.

unresolved_candidates.subject: Where highway conditions permit, warning signs
unresolved_candidates.threshold: Where highway conditions permit, warning signs should be placed in advance of the transition and activity areas at varying distances depending on roadway type, condition, and posted speed. Table 6B-1 contains information regarding the spacing of advance warning signs. Where a series of two or more advance warning signs is used, the closest sign to the transition and activity areas should be placed approximately 100 feet for low-speed urban streets to 1,000 feet or more for freeways and expressways.

unresolved_candidates.subject: Utility, maintenance, and minor construction signing and TTC
unresolved_candidates.threshold: Utility, maintenance, and minor construction signing and TTC should be coordinated with appropriate authorities so that road users are not confused or misled by the additional TTC devices.

unresolved_candidates.subject: The ROAD (STREET) WORK (W20-1) sign (see Figure 6H-1), which serves as a general warning of obstructions or restrictions,
unresolved_candidates.threshold: The ROAD (STREET) WORK (W20-1) sign (see Figure 6H-1), which serves as a general warning of obstructions or restrictions, should be located in advance of the work space or any detour, on the road where the work is taking place.

unresolved_candidates.subject: Where traffic can enter a TTC zone from a crossroad or a major (high-volume) driveway, an advance warning sign
unresolved_candidates.threshold: Where traffic can enter a TTC zone from a crossroad or a major (high-volume) driveway, an advance warning sign should be used on the crossroad or major driveway.

unresolved_candidates.subject: For a single lane closure, the Lane Closed (W20-5) sign (see Figure 6H-1)
unresolved_candidates.threshold: For a single lane closure, the Lane Closed (W20-5) sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall use the legend RIGHT (LEFT) LANE CLOSED. Where two or more adjacent lanes are closed, the W20-5a sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall use the legend XX RIGHT (LEFT) LANES CLOSED.

unresolved_candidates.subject: The Interior Lane Shift (W9-3) sign (see Figure 6H-1)
unresolved_candidates.threshold: The Interior Lane Shift (W9-3) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used in advance of that point where work occupies an interior lane(s) and approaching motor vehicle traffic is directed to the right or left of the work zone in the lane(s) by using a shifting taper to route traffic around the closed interior lane(s).

unresolved_candidates.subject: The MERGE HERE TAKE TURNS (W9-2a) sign (see Figure 6H-1)
unresolved_candidates.threshold: The MERGE HERE TAKE TURNS (W9-2a) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used to identify the merge point at which vehicles from alternate lanes take turns merging during Late Merge applications (see Section 6N.19).

unresolved_candidates.subject: When channelizing devices have the potential of leading vehicular traffic out of the intended vehicular traffic space as shown in Figure 6P-39, the channelizing devices
unresolved_candidates.threshold: When channelizing devices have the potential of leading vehicular traffic out of the intended vehicular traffic space as shown in Figure 6P-39, the channelizing devices should be extended a distance in feet of 2 times the speed limit in mph beyond the downstream end of the transition area.

unresolved_candidates.subject: The appropriate taper length (L)
unresolved_candidates.threshold: The appropriate taper length (L) should 60 be determined using the criteria shown in 45 mph or more L = WS Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4. Where: L = taper length in feet Support: W = width of offset in feet A merging taper requires the longest distance S = posted speed limit, or off‑peak 85th‑percentile speed

unresolved_candidates.subject: A merging taper
unresolved_candidates.threshold: A merging taper should be long enough to enable merging drivers to have adequate advance warning and sufficient length to adjust their speeds and merge into an adjacent lane before the downstream end of the transition.

unresolved_candidates.subject: A shifting taper
unresolved_candidates.threshold: A shifting taper should have a length of approximately ½ L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4).

unresolved_candidates.subject: If used, shoulder tapers
unresolved_candidates.threshold: If used, shoulder tapers should have a length of approximately ¹⁄3 L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4). If a shoulder is used as a travel lane, either through practice or during a TTC activity, a normal merging or shifting taper should be used.

unresolved_candidates.subject: If used, a downstream taper
unresolved_candidates.threshold: If used, a downstream taper should have a minimum length of 50 feet and a maximum length of 100 feet with devices placed at a spacing of approximately 20 feet.

unresolved_candidates.subject: A taper having a minimum length of 50 feet and a maximum length of 100 feet with channelizing devices at approximately 20-foot spacing
unresolved_candidates.threshold: A taper having a minimum length of 50 feet and a maximum length of 100 feet with channelizing devices at approximately 20-foot spacing should be used to guide traffic into the one-lane section, and a downstream taper should be used to guide traffic back into their original lane.

unresolved_candidates.subject: An arrow board in the arrow or chevron mode
unresolved_candidates.threshold: An arrow board in the arrow or chevron mode should be used to advise approaching traffic of a lane closure along major multi-lane roadways in situations involving heavy traffic volumes, high speeds, and/or limited sight distances, or at other locations and under other conditions where road users are less likely to expect such lane closures. Sect. 6L.05 to 6L.06 December 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition Page 833

unresolved_candidates.subject: An arrow board in the arrow or chevron mode
unresolved_candidates.threshold: An arrow board in the arrow or chevron mode shall be used only for stationary or moving lane closures on multi-lane roadways.

unresolved_candidates.subject: For shoulder work, for blocking the shoulder, for roadside work near the shoulder, or for temporarily closing one lane on a two-lane, two-way roadway, an arrow board
unresolved_candidates.threshold: For shoulder work, for blocking the shoulder, for roadside work near the shoulder, or for temporarily closing one lane on a two-lane, two-way roadway, an arrow board shall be used only in the caution mode.

unresolved_candidates.subject: For a stationary lane closure, the arrow board
unresolved_candidates.threshold: For a stationary lane closure, the arrow board should be located on the shoulder at the beginning of the merging taper.

unresolved_candidates.subject: Where the shoulder is narrow, the arrow board
unresolved_candidates.threshold: Where the shoulder is narrow, the arrow board should be located in the closed lane. December 2023 Sect. 6L.06 Page 834 MUTCD 11th Edition Figure 6L-3. Advance Warning Arrow Board Display Specifications Operating Mode Display (Type C arrow board illustrated)

unresolved_candidates.subject: When arrow boards are used to close multiple lanes, a separate arrow board
unresolved_candidates.threshold: When arrow boards are used to close multiple lanes, a separate arrow board shall be used for each closed lane.

unresolved_candidates.subject: When arrow boards are used to close multiple lanes, if the first arrow board is placed on the shoulder, the second arrow board
unresolved_candidates.threshold: When arrow boards are used to close multiple lanes, if the first arrow board is placed on the shoulder, the second arrow board should be placed in the first closed lane at the upstream end of the second merging taper (see Figure 6P-37). When the first arrow board is placed in the first closed lane, the second arrow board should be placed in the second closed lane at the downstream end of the second merging taper. Sect. 6L.06 December 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition Page 835

unresolved_candidates.subject: For mobile operations where a lane is closed, the arrow board
unresolved_candidates.threshold: For mobile operations where a lane is closed, the arrow board should be located to provide adequate separation from the work operation to allow for appropriate reaction by approaching drivers.

unresolved_candidates.subject: Arrow boards
unresolved_candidates.threshold: Arrow boards shall only be used to indicate a lane closure. Arrow boards shall not be used to indicate a lane shift.
